page: Google Cloud Platform ct5l-hightpu-4t is an accelerator-optimized instance tailored for machine learning computation within the GCP TPU family. The host system integrates 112 dedicated virtual CPUs built on the x86_64 architecture, paired with 192 GB of system RAM. This provides approximately 1.71 GB of host memory per vCPU, establishing a high-concurrency host configuration where processor throughput is prioritized to maintain fast data ingestion and batch scheduling pipelines.

At the core of the configuration are 4 Google TPU v5e processing units, offering a combined 64 GB of specialized accelerator memory. TPU v5e processors are purpose-built application-specific integrated circuits designed for matrix operations and tensor mathematics. The instance operates without bundled local disk storage, requiring external persistent network storage solutions for the operating system and data persistence, and it is provisioned with zero default complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an efficiency standpoint, coupling 4 TPU v5e chips with a 112-vCPU host delivers favorable resource density for throughput-critical machine learning workloads without the infrastructure overhead of multi-node TPU pods. The primary trade-off involves the lean memory-to-core ratio of 1.71 GB per vCPU and the lack of high-speed local NVMe storage, meaning memory-intensive host applications or unoptimized I/O pipelines must rely on network storage throughput. The instance is suited for AI model inference serving, medium-scale neural network training, parameter fine-tuning, and parallelized data preparation pipelines.

Hardware acceleration is delivered by 4 integrated Google TPU v5e chips offering a cumulative 64 GB of TPU memory. The instance contains no bundled local disk storage, necessitating network storage attachments for operating system hosting and dataset access, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With a dense host CPU allocation, the server facilitates concurrent data preprocessing, batch pipelining, and runtime orchestration alongside accelerator tasks. From an architectural perspective, the balance of 4 TPU v5e chips and substantial host compute resources yields a cost-effective platform for distributed training, model fine-tuning, and large-scale inference without requiring full-scale pod infrastructure.
